text.p: The probability of New York State getting a budget by its deadline is "essentially zero," state Comptroller H. Carl McCall said Wednesday.
"I'm a realist," McCall said in a statement. "I fully recognize that the probability of an on-time budget this year is essentaiily zero."
The state's fiscal year begins April 1.
He said it is now 12 days until the state sees its 13th consecutive late budget. In 1996, the state set a record for tardiness, passing a budget in mid-summer.
McCall said state lawmakers have not developed a consensus revenue forecast, dooming the state to a late budget.
And McCall, a Democrat, criticized Republican Gov. George Pataki, saying he has been travelling out of state instead of negotiating the budget with lawmakers.
A spokesman for Gov. Pataki was not immediately available for comment.
